Why hasn't the commercial market moved to fiber optic network equipment?What is ultimately the limiting factor?
Lack of competition and already existing networks in place.
TIme and Money. The cost to run fiber throughout a commercial space of say.... 500+ people is huge, especially if they're using outdated cat5 lines.
The city I live in has fiber interwebz. 1 Gbps connection is the best. But only one company I think has it here...

Biggest reason is cost.

Fiber is super cheap. BUT! The gear you put on each end of the fiber is super expensive. Reasons, more complex, faster electronics, electro optic modulators, high speed DACs and ADCs, laser diodes and photodetectors.

Comparatively ethernet uses low speed, super cheap microprocessors that do everything. Everything stays digital, medium changes are expensive.

With fiber you get a network that costs more to setup, uses more power and gives you speeds that are too fast for the best ssd to handle. On top of that fiber is finicky, needs to be cleaned before connection, dirt can mess up you signal and be very hard to find, small bends can crack and degrade the fibre. You need to know what you are doing, it's not plug and play like ethernet usually is. Of course on any large distance or large haul networking, fiber works wonders.

There are 2 reasons we might make the switch from ethernet to fiber are. Optical computing, if that ever takes off or, quantum key exchange immune mitm attacks.

To add to this, there's also little competition in most areas of the USA due to govt subsidized monopolies for internet service. This makes it even more costly for any potential competition to roll out fiber. Especially in sparsely populated areas, the govt subsidies can exceed the cost in and of themselves (i.e. telcos could give service away and still turn a profit - and fiber can't compete with "free").

Basically what /u/Dimand said. The cost of going out and augmenting/replacing thousands of Miles of copper cable with Fiber is daunting. The actual cable, the equipment and major nodes, etc. is minimal, compared to the cost of personnel and equipment to go out and either add to or pull down and replace lines on poles, or dig up cables already laid in the ground and replace them with new cables.

My comment was more aimed at a home or office environment network.

Any new service network should be fiber in my opinion. For long links (say the 2km to your local exchange) then copper is hard pressed to do any better than adsl2+.

The fiber to the home NBN project in aus, while a huge infrastructure project, is a great idea and needed as the copper is failing us right now.

Big telecom companies were given tax dollars to do this exact thing. But nope. They just hoard cash.

Edit: Evidence of this was seen when Google fiber was intoduced to certain cities. Telecom companies immediately began boosting speeds. In short, we dont have fiber because the telecom companies don't have to install it. They still have the same customers. What we do need is either regulation or competiton.
Ultimately cost and building out infrastructure. Companies want to make the most of existing/old infrastructure for as long as they possibly can..
